City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
April 2, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:03 p.m. , on April 2, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on March 28, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley
RECESS AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winners
Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented the senior single family residence Recycling Program Award to Suzanne and John Popel.
P2.
O.C. Crime Stoppers
The City Council received the presentation from Aaron Berenschot, OC Crime Stoppers Coordinator.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that a majority of the citizens do not want a million dollar dog park and that any excess monies should be used to reduce the City's burdens or saved for a disaster. Larry Gilbert, M.V.: discussed the recent meeting of the RDA Successor Agency's Oversight Board and he noted that he has filed a complaint with the Stated Department of Finance .
The following expressed support for a Mission Viejo Dog Park: Victoria Avery, M.V.; Barbara Losee, M.V.; Dan Avery, M.V.; Nermine Morcos, M.V.; Janis Kosmala, M.V.; Nancy Chontos, M.V.; Susan Sellers, M.V.; Carissa Sellers, M.V.; Joey Sellers, M.V.; Dorrie Steele, M.V.; and Daniel Futterman, M.V.
The following expressed concern for a Dog Park at the proposed location and at the proposed cost: Carol Schwimmer, M.V.; Gail Reavis, M.V.; Erin Walker, M.V.; and Dr. Michael Ferrall, M.V.
The following presented a written comment in opposition to a dog park adjacent to Quail Run: Steven Schwimmer.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 7, 9, and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 19, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register Dated March 9, 2012 in the Amount of $1,693,894.35
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated March 16, 2012 in the amount of $898,545.19
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2012-2013 Detailing Cityâ??s Proposed Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds
Adopted Resolution 12-18 Approving the City’s Draft Annual Action Plan for FY 2012-2013 Detailing the City's Proposed Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of Such Plans to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
6.
Measure M2 Tier 1 Round 2 Environmental Clean-Up Program Applications
Adopted Resolution 12-19 Authorizing the City Manager to Apply for Funds for the Environmental Cleanup Tier 1 Grant Program Under Orange County Local Transportation Ordinance No. 3 for the La Paz Road, Alicia Parkway, and Santa Margarita Parkway Median Island Runoff Prevention Projects.
8.
Authorization to Bid Marguerite Parkway Median Island Landscape Improvements
Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids the Marguerite Parkway Median Island Landscape Renovation (CIP 799) from Mesilla to La Sierra.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
11.
Amendment to conditions of approval for Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 - Request submitted by UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP, to modify the applicable conditions of approval in previously approved City Council Resolution No. 11-54 approving Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 for the construction of a three-level multifamily complex on 10.83 acres at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) zone. The subject application is a request to modify the project approval by eliminating the requirement that 48 units be reserved as affordable housing units
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report. Planning Manager Elaine Lister provided background on the proposed project and on affordable housing. She also outlined the RHNA Allocation Plan for Mission Viejo.
Don MacKenzie, Managing Director of UDR Development: discussed UDR’s request to modify the conditions of approval and eliminate the requirement that 48 units be reserved for affordable housing.
The following spoke in opposition to the removal of the affordable housing requirement: Gail Reavis, M.V. and Harry Lynczk, M.V.
Mr. MacKenzie provided rebuttal comments and answered questions of the City Council.
Council Member Reardon noted that during her last meeting with UDR representatives, she told the developers that she hoped they had a strategy in the event that redevelopment funds might go away.
Council Member Kelley stated that the Planning Commission vote was weak due to the absence of two Commissioners and she expressed her hesitance to remove the affordable units from this project. She reminded UDR representatives that they knew that redevelopment funding was in question.
Council Member Schlicht stated that she cannot support removing the affordable component for this project. She later noted that she is against social engineering however she is not afraid of affordable housing.
Mayor Ury stated that it is disingenuous for a Council Member to require affordable housing at this project after generally opposing affordable housing in the past. He expressed concern that the UDR may increase the density of the project and he stated that the Council has the ability to control density with its vote tonight.
Council Member Leckness stated that his biggest concern is the developer’s legal ability to add density to the project and increase the number of units if the Council rejects the request tonight.
Mr. MacKenzie asked the Council Members for guidance and whether they want affordability or density.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution 12-XX Approving a Request Submitted by UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP, to Modify the Applicable Conditions of Approval in Previously Approved City Council Resolution No. 11-54 Approving Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 for the Construction of a Three-Level Multifamily Complex on 10.83 acres at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) zone, by Eliminating the Requirement that 48 Units be Reserved as Affordable Housing Units.
On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury.
NOES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
ABSENT:
None
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to deny the request submitted by UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP, to modify the applicable conditions of approval in previously approved City Council Resolution No. 11-54 approving Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 for the construction of a three-level multifamily complex on 10.83 acres at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) zone, by eliminating the requirement that 48 units be reserved as affordable housing units, subject to a confirming resolution at the next City Council meeting.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
ABSENT:
None
RECESS
At the hour of 8:10 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:21 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
9.
Mission Viejo Library Story Time Room Remodel (CIP 601)
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: expressed concern with the proposed costs for the Story Time Room remodel project.
Library Director Stephanie Tanton answered questions of the City Council.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to award the contract for the subject project to Optima RPM, Inc. in the amount of $358,344.
On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, and Mayor Ury.
NOES:
Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
ABSENT:
None
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to postpone the item for 30 days and return to the City Council at the first meeting in May.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
Mayor Ury
ABSENT:
None
OLD BUSINESS
12.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report and he answered the City Council Member's questions.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) approve Change Order No.8 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in an amount $61,569.04; (2) approve Change Order No.4 to RJM Design Group for design changes in the amount $30,810; and (3) approve Change Order No.1 to Petra Geotechnical, Incorporated for geotechnical field observations and inspections for design change in the amount of $45,219.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
NEW BUSINESS
13.
Public Scoping Meeting for the Preparation of an Environmental Impact Report Related to the City’s Comprehensive Update to the General Plan
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
John Bridges, AECOM: discussed the General Plan Update and Sustainability Action Plan EIR.
Laura Jacksen, M.V.: expressed her interest in the plan and requested improvement in the reduction of single driver vehicle traffic. She also recommended enhancing bike trails and paths, training residents and providing incentives for household sustainability and full use of reusable containers and bags.
14.
Presentation by Representatives from AECOM Regarding Preliminary Findings and Recommendations Concerning the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Plan Accompanying the General Plan Update
Jeff Henderson, AECOM: provided an overview of the Sustainability Action Plan which will be prepared in tandem with the General Plan Update and EIR.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)
7.
First Amendment to Consultant Services Agreement with Eric Winter for MVTV Production Services
Council Member Schlicht indicated that she will vote against this contract amendment because she feels that the budget was ignored.
City Clerk/Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman outlined recent improvements to MVTV programming and she highlighted viewership statistics in comparison with other local government channels. She noted that staff hopes to continue increasing and improving programming for MVTV.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the First Amendment to the Consultant Services Agreement with Eric Winter for Television Production Services in the amount of $13,600 (A12-09A.)
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
10.
Award of Independent Auditor Contract for Fiscal Years Ending June 30, 2012 and 2013
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas explained the reason for changing auditors and answered questions of the City Council.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
15.
CUSD Ad Hoc Committee Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
16.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he has been unable to obtain dispatch reports from the Orange County Fire Authority just as the LA Times has been unable to obtain dispatch records from the Los Angeles Fire Department.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
17.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA.
18.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Council Member Reardon presented the report.
Council Member Schlicht left the room at 10:29 p.m. and returned at 10:31 p.m.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Manager Wilberg noted that the Oversight Board of the Successor Agency for the Mission Viejo Redevelopment Agency held its first meeting last week. Mr. Wilberg asked the Council Members if they would like a report of the Oversight Board Meetings on the Council Agendas or a copy of the Minutes via email. Mayor Ury indicated that he would prefer that the Council receive verbal reports at the Council Meetings during the City Manager’s Report.
City Attorney’s Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
19.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at Olympian and Author Kristi Yamaguchi’s presentation of her new children’s book. She thanked Library Director Stephanie Tanton for arranging to bring Mrs. Yamaguchi to Mission Viejo for the second time. She also attended the Tee it Up Fore Marines Golf Tournament dinner and she commended staff and the Marine Adoption Committee for their hard work in making the event so successful. Council Member Kelley also attended the annual Saddleback College gala fundraiser and she thanked the community for their support in raising money for Saddleback College. Mrs. Kelley announced that there will be a Red Cross Blood Drive at City Hall on Wednesday, April 4, 2012, from 12:30 to 6:30 p.m. Those interested in donating blood can sign up on line or call her for an appointment. Also, on Saturday, April 7, the City will hold its annual Bunny Days event from 11:00 to 2:00 p.m. and she encouraged residents to attend. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of April is service and she concluded her comments with a quote from Mother Teresa: "Never worry about numbers. Help one person at a time, and always start with the person nearest you."
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness asked Council Members Reardon and Schlicht how much they would be comfortable spending on a dog park. Council Member Reardon responded that she feels $100,000 is more than enough to build a dog park.
Council Member Leckness asked Council Member Kelley to resign from the Orange County Parks Board or not reapply when her term is up in May so she can put her interests in the City above the County and vote on the dog park.
Council Member Kelley replied that she recused herself from the dog park vote after she received legal advice from the City Attorney and the County Counsel. She stated that she feels that it is very good to have Council members sitting on regional boards and she has worked very hard, on behalf of Mission Viejo, during her time on the County Parks Commission. She further stated that she does not put the County above the City. Council Member Kelley noted that the City Attorney can write a letter to the FPPC asking for an opinion on whether or not she truly needs to recuse herself from the dog park County land swap vote and she asked City Attorney Curley to work with her on that letter.
Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at recent events including the Ms. Senior Orange County Pageant at the Murray Center and a Persian New Year celebration at Comerica Bank. Lastly, he discussed the annual Chamber of Commerce breakfast and he thanked Mayor Ury for speaking at the event.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht recognized the upcoming holy week and she wished residents a happy Easter. She reminded the community that the Chamber of Commerce will host a free Tedx simulcast, live from Berlin, in the Council Chamber on Thursday April 5, 2012, from 7:30 to 10:30 a.m. Council Member Schlicht also announced that the next Chamber mixer will be held on April 19 at the Rampage Fitness Academy on Via Linda and she invited residents to a Tea Party peaceful protest on the corners of La Paz and Marguerite on Monday, April 16. Council Member Schlicht concluded with a quote from Thomas Paine: "Reputation is what men and women think of us; character is what God and angels know of us."
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon stated that the Council Members need to ask questions instead of making assumptions, statements and judgments. She noted that she is not against dogs being off leash in a legal way but she thinks that the Council is going about a dog park in the wrong way. She inquired about previous quotes to develop a dog park at Oso Viejo Park and she thanked the residents who came out tonight, and those who email her, for expressing their opinions. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her participation as Principal for a Day at Del Lago Elementary School. It is a very diverse school and she was so impressed with the PTA’s work to raise funds for the school. It also opened her eyes to what can be done with volunteer fundraising at a time when the City is considering spending $1 million on a dog park. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her attendance at the Tee it Up Fore Marines golf tournament and she thanked Council Member Kelley for the initial idea to adopt a Marine battalion. She noted that the Marines and their families are so grateful for the services and money that the Adoption Committee provides. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon also visited a Mission Viejo Christian School event where she learned that each student has adopted a cancer patient and it was compelling to see the efforts of these young people who raised $3,186 for cancer research. She stated that there are a lot of wonderful things going on and she is becoming more and more enamored with the people of this community who are doing things on their own to give back. Lastly, Council Member Reardon announced that the City will screen a movie about the prescription drug overdose epidemic in Orange County on April 26, 2012, at the Murray Community Center and more information will follow.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury reminded his colleagues that the City has been working on a dog park since 2002 and he is disappointed that ten years’ worth of work was shot down at the last meeting. He stated that talking is easy and leadership is tough, and the good things that have been done in the past seem to be ignored. Mayor Ury announced that he was unable to attend the Marine benefit golf tournament but he heard it was a great event. He also discussed his attendance at the annual Chamber of Commerce breakfast and he thanked Council Member Leckness for doing a great job as the MC. Mayor Ury outlined the challenges that he presented at the Chamber breakfast to encourage the City Council Members to spend more time on Economic Development and business retention.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 11:10 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 16, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of April 16, 2012
